metadata.title: Lingo Agent
metadata.description: An open-source AI English tutor that remembers you.

home.badge: Open source · Self-hostable · Bring your own models
home.title: Your AI English tutor
home.subtitle: It remembers what you know and what you keep getting wrong.
home.note: Works from A1 to C2. Explanations can lean on Chinese or stay all in English.

demo.label: Example conversation
demo.user: Yesterday I go to a job interview and I was very nervous.
demo.reply: Good luck with the job hunt! One small fix: I went to a job interview — “yesterday” needs the past tense.
demo.replyNote: You wrote go in the present tense last time too. I've noted it and we'll practise it again next week.
demo.memory: Read: you're preparing for an interview at the end of October

memory.title: A tutor that remembers you
memory.body: Your goals, interests and usual mistakes. Each chat picks up where you left off, so you never have to introduce yourself again.

grammar.title: Grammar tracking and mastery
grammar.body: Every grammar point has a mastery level and the evidence behind it: which sentence went wrong, which time you got it right.

vocab.title: FSRS vocabulary
vocab.body: Oxford 3000, CET-4/6, IELTS and more, reviewed on an FSRS spaced-repetition schedule. New words from your chats can go in too.

placement.title: Placement test
placement.body: About 10 minutes for a CEFR level and an estimated vocabulary size. The tutor pitches its explanations at your level.

transparency.title: See everything the AI does
transparency.body: Every button that calls a model is marked AI; open it to see which model and roughly how many tokens. What the tutor read and saved unfolds under each reply.

models.title: Your models, self-hosted
models.body: Connect DeepSeek, OpenAI, Anthropic, Qwen, SiliconFlow and more. Runs on a small server, and your data stays with you.

trust.eyebrow: Transparency is the core of this product
trust.title: Everything the tutor remembers, you can see, edit and delete
trust.body: When the tutor wants to switch your word book or set a goal, it asks first. Nothing changes until you confirm, and you can undo it afterwards.
trust.cardTitle: Switch your word book to IELTS?
trust.cardBody: You mentioned taking IELTS next year. Nothing changes until you confirm.
trust.hint: ← Open the AI mark: which models it calls and roughly how many tokens

connections.confirmDelete: Delete the connection "{name}"? Routes using it will skip it.
connections.defaultModelHint: Chat uses it when no model is set for it. For a connection used only for speech-to-text or images, enter that model and pick the matching test.

connections.ttsNotSupported: This connection can't read aloud (the server has no /audio/speech endpoint, or no such voice). Use a read-aloud model from Azure Speech, SiliconFlow, OpenAI or a local Speaches instead.

source.default: Using the default order from the server configuration.

route.editHint: Pick a connection and a model for each row. The first one is used; the rest take over if it fails.
route.modelsFailed: Couldn't fetch the model list. Type a model name.

chat.title: Chat model
chat.description: Models are tried in order; if one fails, the next one takes over.
chat.none: No chat model is usable yet. Add a connection and save its default model.

reflect.title: Background memory model
reflect.description: Runs after each reply: decides what the tutor should remember about you and writes conversation summaries. A smaller, cheaper model is fine here.
reflect.none: No model available: the tutor won't remember anything new until you add a chat model.

vision.title: Image model (vision)
vision.description: Reads images and scanned PDF pages, and answers messages that carry images. Pick models that can see images: chat models are not used for this automatically.
vision.none: Not set up: images and scanned PDFs can't be read until you add a model here.

asr.title: Speech-to-text
asr.description: Transcribes voice messages and audio files (an OpenAI-compatible /audio/transcriptions API, e.g. Groq, OpenAI, SiliconFlow or a local speaches server).
asr.none: Not set up: voice messages can't be transcribed until you add a model here.

tts.title: Read aloud
tts.description: Reads tutor replies, words and examples with a server voice (Azure Speech, or an OpenAI-compatible /audio/speech endpoint such as SiliconFlow, OpenAI or a local speaches). Sentences already read are cached.
tts.none: Not set up: learners' browsers read aloud.

route.allOff: Every model here is switched off. Turn one on to use this.
route.switchedOff: {ref} is off and will be skipped.
route.voiceNone: No built-in voice: the next model or the browser reads this language
route.voicesHint: Under each model you can choose a voice per language; empty uses the built-in one. An Azure connection offers its voices.

usage.title: Usage
usage.description: Token counts per day and model, as reported by the providers. Prices are not included.
usage.empty: No model calls in this period.

display.title: Display
display.showActivity: Show “What the tutor did” under replies
display.showActivityHint: Memories read and saved, grammar mistakes marked. Hiding it changes the display only: everything is still recorded, and the Memory page still shows it all.

background.title: Background work
background.description: The tutor prepares some things while you are away. Each can be switched off; it is then done when you need it, with a short wait.
background.budgetExhausted: Today's background budget is used up; it resets tomorrow (UTC). What you start yourself still works.
background.budgetOff: An admin switched off all background model calls. What you start yourself still works.

practice_prefetch.name: Prepare the next practice set
practice_prefetch.hint: After you finish a grammar set, the next one is generated in the background so it opens without a wait.

article_prerewrite.name: Rewrite new articles ahead
article_prerewrite.hint: When the feeds you follow have new articles, they are rewritten for your level with comprehension questions in the background, so they open without a wait.

word_examples_prefetch.name: Write AI example sentences ahead
word_examples_prefetch.hint: For words you will review or learn in the next day that have no real example sentence, AI sentences are written in the background, so the card shows them when you turn it over.

diagnosis.name: The tutor's diagnosis
diagnosis.hint: For grammar points you keep getting wrong, the tutor looks for likely root causes in the background, across their prerequisites and the points they are often confused with, quoting your own sentences, and practice brings the related points up more often. Weekly, and after a practice set with many new mistakes.

background.budgetHint: How many tokens background calls (ones no learner is waiting for) may use per day, from midnight UTC. Checked before each piece of background work starts, so the last one may go slightly over. 0 switches all background calls off. Chat, grading and other things learners start are never limited.

skip.budget_exhausted: Today's background budget was used up.

wordAudio.priceHint: Check the vendor's pricing page; the price is only used for the estimate, and without one only characters are shown. Azure's free tier allows 500,000 characters a month and 20 requests a minute; past the limit it waits and tries again.
wordAudio.estimate: {words} words, {pieces} pieces of audio, {existing} already there, {toMake} to generate.
wordAudio.missing: No voice for {accents}; it won't be generated.

placement.title: Placement test
placement.description: About 10 minutes to find your level; your tutor adjusts explanations and practice to it.

intro.vocab: One English word at a time; say whether you know it. Some are made up, so if you don't know a word, answer "No" rather than guess.
intro.grammar: A sentence with one blank; pick the right one of four options.
intro.notes: If unsure, pick what seems most likely; answers are not shown. You can leave at any time and continue later. When you finish, your level is set to the result (you can still change it on the Memory page).

question.grammarPrompt: Choose the option that fills the blank

result.title: Your result
result.levelNote: Your overall level, set by the grammar part. It is saved to your profile, and your tutor adjusts explanations and practice to it.
result.vocabReference: Roughly {level} by vocabulary size (Milton 2010; for reference only, not used for your level)
result.vocabNote: For reference only; not used for your level
result.unreliable: You said you knew quite a few made-up words, so this vocabulary estimate isn't reliable and won't be used to mark words known. For a better estimate, take the test again and answer "No" to words you don't know.
result.nextDescription: Go through the result with your tutor. It goes by your learning data, and anything it proposes waits for your OK.
result.planNote: Not sure where to start? Your tutor goes through the result with you, asks about your goal and time, and suggests a word book, grammar practice and a daily goal. Nothing changes until you confirm it.
result.plan: Talk the result over with the tutor
result.knownTitle: Skip common words you already know
result.knownDescription: From your estimated vocabulary, mark the current book's common words you very likely know as known; they won't come up as new words.
result.retestDescription: A new test replaces your level with its result and adds a new set of placement records. Words already marked known stay as they are.

aiBadge.label: Uses AI: what it does and roughly how many tokens

feature.chat_message: Your tutor's reply is written by an AI model. After it, the tutor reviews the turn in the background to update your memories, mistakes and words. A longer message (60+ English words) is first checked by an AI model to see whether it is your own writing; if so, the writing coach reviews it sentence by sentence.
feature.chat_image: An AI model reads each image first, so the tutor can talk about it. The reply to that message also comes from the image-reading model.
feature.chat_pdf: PDFs with a text layer are read without AI. Scanned pages are read by an AI model, one call per page.
feature.chat_audio: Your recording is turned into text by a speech-to-text model.
feature.practice_start: The tutor opens the practice with a first message written by an AI model.
feature.plan_start: The tutor opens the planning conversation with a first message written by an AI model, from your test result and learning data. After that, each reply is like any chat message.
feature.practice_set: An AI model writes a set of items on your weak grammar points; another model solves and reviews each one first, and items that fail are rewritten. Bank items fill any gaps. After you finish a set, the next one is written in the background.
feature.practice_grade: Open answers (rewrites, translations, fixing your own sentence) and fixes not in an item's answer list are graded by an AI model: it judges the tested grammar point, explains, and points out other grammar mistakes in your answer. Multiple choice and fill-in answers are graded by code, without AI. Only your first answer to each item is graded.
feature.memory_edit: Adding or editing a memory turns it into a vector with an embedding model, so the tutor can find it later.
feature.word_examples: An AI model writes two example sentences for this word at your level. They are saved, so the next time anyone asks for this word at this level, no model is called.
feature.message_translate: An AI model translates this message. The translation is saved, so switching back and forth makes no more calls.
feature.writing_submit: An AI model reviews your writing sentence by sentence: it finds and explains grammar mistakes, scores four aspects, writes overall feedback and puts unknown words on your word list. Mistakes go into your learner model; scores are only shown.
feature.reading_rewrite: An AI model rewrites this article for your level and writes a few comprehension questions; another model answers each question itself to check it, and a question that fails is rewritten once, then dropped. The rewrite is saved: opening it again at the same level calls no model.
feature.reading_coach: The reading coach answers your questions about this article: each message sends the article (the version for your level, or the beginning of the original) with the conversation, so a reply reads more than a chat turn. Afterwards, as in any chat, memory and grammar notes are updated in the background.
feature.reading_prerewrite: In the background every two hours: new articles of the feeds you follow are rewritten for your level with questions, by the same AI calls as opening an article, within the tenant's daily background budget.
feature.word_examples_prefetch: In the background every six hours: for the words you will review or learn in the next day that have no real example sentence, the same AI call as the "AI examples" button writes two sentences at your level, at most 30 words a time, within the tenant's daily background budget. Learners at the same level share them.
feature.diagnosis: In the background at most weekly (also after a practice set with many new mistakes, at most daily): the AI model reads up to 3 grammar points you keep getting wrong, their prerequisites and the points they are often confused with, and your latest mistakes, and suggests root causes. Conclusions that cannot quote your own sentences are dropped. Within the tenant's daily background budget.
feature.read_aloud: Replies, words and examples are read by the server's read-aloud model; sentences already read are cached and not billed again. You can turn it off in the read-aloud settings and use only this device's voices.
feature.word_audio_prefetch: Started by hand in the settings for one word book: the first model in the read-aloud route reads each word in American and/or British English once and the audio is kept, so learners reading a word aloud play it with no model call. Billed by characters, estimated before it starts; not against the daily background budget.
